hook: A $40 hourly rate pays you about $20
hook_say: Here is what a $40 hourly rate really pays a service business owner.

rows.label: Rate you quote per billed hour
rows.why: Start with the rate you quote: $40 for every hour you bill.

rows.label: Unbilled hours (quotes, driving, admin)
rows.why: Quoting, driving and admin eat about 1 of every 3 hours you work, and nobody pays for those.

rows.label: Overhead per month
rows.why: Add $500 a month of overhead: insurance, supplies, phone, software.

rows.label: Hours worked per month
rows.why: Spread that over 150 working hours a month.

rows.label: Kept per hour worked
rows.why: After unpaid hours, overhead and self-employment tax, you keep about $20 for every hour worked. Half the rate is gone before income tax.

fix.label: To keep $30 an hour, bill
fix.why: To keep $30 an hour worked, the same business needs to bill about $57. The calculator does this math for your numbers.

note: Example numbers. Your own go in the calculator.
